chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman who runs between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. He said: Yes, by my life, the Messenger of Allah commanded Asma' bint Umays to perform Ghusl, use Istithfar (place a cloth to stop the flow), and perform Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwah.

key_terms.استَثفَرَت: She used Istithfar (placed a cloth to stop menstrual flow)
key_terms.الصّفَا وَ المَروَة: As-Safa and Al-Marwah (the hills in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: Can a menstruating woman perform Tawaf between Safa and Marwah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies that menstruation does not invalidate the Tawaf of the Prophet (peace be upon him) for Umrah, as evidenced by Asma' bint Umays being commanded to perform Ghusl and Istithfar before completing her circuit. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the barrier (Istithfar) allows for ritual purity sufficient for Tawaf even during menstruation, distinguishing it from the state of major impurity that might otherwise hinder worship. This precedent underscores the flexibility in ritual obligations when facing natural biological states, ensuring the completion of Umrah rites without delay.
